title: {{NAME}} and the Match of Two Worlds
moral: When two very different worlds play together, both come away richer.

pages.content:
The Annual Cross-World Exhibition Match was the hero guild's most popular charity event.

This year's twist: the fairy team from Thornwood had challenged the junior heroes.

Fairy football was played by different rules: no offside, aerial possession allowed within one body-length of the fairy's own height, and the ball could be charmed once per half.

{{NAME}} was the heroes' captain. The ball had been charmed three times in the pre-match warm-up, twice making it spin the wrong direction and once making it turn purple.

"It goes back to normal," the fairy captain assured him.

"Does it?" said {{NAME}}.

pages.content:
He spent the week before the match on rule analysis.

The fairy team's advantage: the charm. Used strategically, it could destabilise any set move.

Defence against the charm: improvisation-based play, where the heroes practiced responding to random changes rather than set positions.

Offence: the heroes' physical pace exceeded the fairies' in ground situations. If they could keep the ball on the ground and play fast, the aerial rule barely mattered.

"We play our game," he told the team. "Fast. Ground. React to everything."

pages.content:
Match day: extraordinary.

The fairy team used the charm at the 34th minute when {{NAME}}'s team was about to score: the ball turned oval for thirty seconds, which was genuinely disorienting.

{{NAME}}'s team adapted. You can still kick an oval ball if you adjust your foot angle.

The second charm came at the 67th minute and made the ball weightless for sixty seconds, drifting slowly wherever it pointed.

The fairy team thought this would cause chaos. What it actually caused was a slow-motion passing game that {{NAME}}'s team, calmer than expected, enjoyed enormously.

pages.content:
Final score: three all.

The fairy captain and {{NAME}} shook hands at the centre circle.

"You adapted to the charm," she said. "Both times."

"You had better aerial skills," he said. "Three out of our four goals came from you ignoring our defenders and flying over them."

They looked at each other.

"Same time next year?" she asked.

"With one change," said {{NAME}}. "We get one charm too."

She considered this.

"Done," she said.

pages.content:
He walked home with his medal and the memory of the weightless ball drifting through the air.

The thing nobody planned: the slow-motion passing sequence during the second charm had been the most beautiful football he had ever played.

Not despite the strange rules. Because of them.

He thought: sometimes the best games are the ones where you don't know exactly what's coming.

In bed, he lay smiling at the ceiling, turning the medal over in his hand.

Next year, he was already planning what to do with his own charm.
